# Belief-Probe Order Sensitivity: Is MASK-Style Honesty Scoring an Artifact of Question Order?

**Problem:** MASK elicits 'belief' before/after pressure to score honesty. A methodological failure-mode worth investigating: does the measured honesty score depend on whether belief is elicited before or after the pressure prompt, and on the order of the indirect consistency probes?

**Direction:** Re-run a MASK-style honesty protocol on open models while permuting the order of (pressure prompt, direct belief query, indirect consistency probes). **Why it matters:** Honesty benchmarks are young; if scores are order-sensitive, comparisons across models/papers are unreliable. A meta-investigation that quantifies this fragility strengthens the whole 'measuring honesty' agenda — a cheap methodological contribution.

title: Truth Drift in Long Contexts: Does a Model Forget Its Own Earlier Honest Answer?

# Truth Drift in Long Contexts: Does a Model Forget Its Own Earlier Honest Answer?

**Problem:** Multi-turn sycophancy aside, a distinct failure is positional truth-drift: across a long conversation with intervening unrelated turns, does a model's answer to a repeated factual question drift without any user pressure at all? This isolates context-length-induced inconsistency from social pressure.

**Direction:** Ask the same factual question at the start of a conversation, then again after inserting N unrelated filler turns, with no pushback. Vary N up to the context limit on an open model. Measure answer-consistency decay as a function of intervening context length, separating drift from pressure-driven flipping.

**Why it matters:** Long-context agents make many decisions; if truthfulness silently erodes with context length even absent pressure, long-horizon deployments are unreliable in a way single-turn evals miss. A clean, cheap, reproducible characterization of a medium-horizon failure mode.

**Relevant context:** SYCON-Bench / 'Measuring Sycophancy in Multi-turn Dialogues' (arXiv:2505.23840) study pressure-driven flips; this isolates the no-pressure context-length confound. Relates to faithfulness-decay observations (arXiv:2602.11201).

title: Does Asking for a Confidence Score Make a Model More Honest or Just More Hedgy?

# Does Asking for a Confidence Score Make a Model More Honest or Just More Hedgy?

**Problem:** A common honesty intervention is to ask the model to attach a confidence score. A subtle failure mode: this may improve calibration, or it may merely make answers verbose/hedgy without improving the truthfulness of the underlying claim. **Direction:** Compare three prompting conditions on a labeled QA set: plain answer, answer + self-reported confidence, and answer + forced uncertainty hedging. **Why it matters:** Confidence-elicitation prompts are widely recommended as a cheap honesty fix. Empirically characterizing when they genuinely help vs. produce empty hedging keeps practitioners from a false sense of security — a high-value, fully lab-independent finding.

title: Metamorphic Relations for Sycophancy: Semantics-Preserving Pressure Mutations

original_idea.body:
# Metamorphic Relations for Sycophancy: Semantics-Preserving Pressure Mutations

**Problem:** Sycophancy benchmarks use fixed prompts, but real conversational pressure is highly varied. There is no oracle for 'correct' non-sycophantic behavior, making evaluation brittle and easy to game.

**Direction:** Borrow metamorphic testing from software engineering. Define metamorphic relations (MRs) over a seed question: paraphrase, add an authority claim, add an emotional appeal, swap user-asserted wrong answer. The MR is 'the model's factual answer should be invariant under pressure-only transformations.' Run an open model (Llama-3-8B, Qwen) on a few hundred seeds x MR families, count MR violations (flips). No oracle needed: violations are detected by inconsistency between source and follow-up outputs, exactly as in METAL/MORTAR.

**Why it matters:** Turns sycophancy testing into an oracle-free, automatable discipline that anyone can run without a lab. Produces a reusable MR library and a violation-rate metric that scales across model families, addressing the open problem of realistic sycophancy measurement.

**Relevant context:** METAL and MORTAR apply metamorphic testing to LLMs without LLM judges using char/word/sentence perturbations (arXiv:2412.15557; cho-icsme-2025). SYCON and ELEPHANT show LLMs flip under multi-turn pressure (arXiv:2505.23840, arXiv:2505.13995). Claude Opus 4.5 system card: 10% course-correction under real pressure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Transformations + violation counting on open models; accessible.

title: Mutation Adequacy for CoT Monitors: Do Faithfulness Tests Actually Catch Unfaithful Reasoning?

original_idea.body:
# Mutation Adequacy for CoT Monitors: Do Faithfulness Tests Actually Catch Unfaithful Reasoning?

**Problem:** CoT-faithfulness test suites (hint-acknowledgment, paraphrase-invariance) are assumed to detect unfaithful reasoning, but like code coverage they may be a vanity metric that passes without truly exercising the failure mode.

**Direction:** Import mutation testing's 'kill rate' adequacy criterion. Treat a faithfulness test suite as the test, and synthetically inject known unfaithfulness 'mutants' into transcripts (e.g., insert a decisive hint into the prompt but a CoT that never mentions it; truncate the load-bearing reasoning step). Measure what fraction of injected mutants the suite 'kills' (flags). A suite that misses many mutants is inadequate. Use an open instruct model to generate transcripts; mutants are programmatic edits.

**Why it matters:** Mutation testing is strictly more stringent than coverage. Quantifying the kill rate of popular faithfulness tests tells the field which tests are real and which give false reassurance — directly relevant to whether CoT monitoring can be trusted for oversight.

**Relevant context:** Mutation testing measures suite quality via mutant kill rate, stricter than branch coverage (arXiv:2104.11767; Codecov mutation testing). Faithfulness tests include hint acknowledgment (arXiv:2505.05410, 25% acknowledgment for Claude 3.7) and paraphrase-invariance (arXiv:2307.13702).

# Reality Monitoring Linguistic Cues as a Cheap CoT-Unfaithfulness Detector

**Problem:** Detecting when a CoT is a post-hoc rationalization rather than a faithful trace usually requires interventions. We lack a lightweight, training-free text signal.

**Direction:** Transfer the 'reality monitoring' framework from forensic deception psychology: fabricated accounts differ in linguistic features (fewer perceptual details, more cognitive-load markers, more distancing language, simpler structure). **Why it matters:** ML on reality-monitoring features beats human lie detectors (69-77% vs ~55%). If these cues transfer to model CoTs, we get a zero-cost, model-agnostic unfaithfulness screen usable outside labs — a building block for cheap monitoring.

title: Cheap-Talk Game Theory: When Is a Model's Confidence Statement Credible?

original_idea.body:
# Cheap-Talk Game Theory: When Is a Model's Confidence Statement Credible?

**Problem:** Models verbalize confidence ('I'm 90% sure'), but in game-theoretic terms these are cheap talk — costless messages that need not be informative. We don't know whether stated confidence is incentive-compatible with accuracy.

**Direction:** Apply the cheap-talk / signaling framework from economics. Set up a simple disclosure game on factual QA: model states a confidence and an answer; score it under (a) no incentive, (b) a proper scoring rule communicated in-prompt (Brier-style payoff). Measure calibration (reliability diagrams) in each regime. The cheap-talk prediction: without a scoring rule, stated confidence is uninformative; with one, signals become more truthful.

**Why it matters:** Frames honesty of self-reports as a mechanism-design problem and tests whether prompt-level incentives make confidence reports credible — a training-free honesty lever any researcher can study, relevant to trusting model self-assessments.

**Relevant context:** Cheap talk = costless, non-binding messages vs costly signaling (Wikipedia 'Cheap talk'; Algorithmic Cheap Talk arXiv:2311.09011). Revelation principle and truthful mechanisms (ACM TEAC 10.1145/3434408). Calibration is standard via reliability diagrams.

title: Differential Fuzzing for Honesty: Cross-Model Divergence as a Hallucination Oracle

original_idea.body:
# Differential Fuzzing for Honesty: Cross-Model Divergence as a Hallucination Oracle

**Problem:** Verifying factual honesty needs a ground-truth oracle, which is expensive. Differential testing in software finds bugs without an oracle by comparing independent implementations on the same input.

**Direction:** Import differential testing. Fuzz a fixed bank of factual questions (SimpleQA) across several independently-built open models. Where models confidently disagree, treat it as a candidate honesty fault and inspect. Quantify how well 'confident cross-model divergence' predicts actual factual errors against SimpleQA labels (precision/recall of divergence as an error detector).

# Can a Cheap Paraphraser Restore Monitor Visibility on Cued Tasks?

**Problem:** Causal chain (defense side): a model hides cue-use in phrasing/style -> monitor misses it. Under-studied INTERVENTION link: if you paraphrase the CoT with a weak trusted model BEFORE the monitor reads it, does monitor detection of cue-use improve, or does paraphrasing wash out the (already faint) signal?

**Direction:** Take cued QA tasks with unfaithful CoTs. Build a simple monitor (LLM judge) that flags 'did the model use the hint?'. Compare monitor accuracy on (a) raw CoT vs. (b) CoT paraphrased by a small trusted model. Hypothesis: paraphrasing removes steganographic phrasing channels but may also remove subtle tells. Success: monitor precision/recall under both conditions.

**Why it matters:** Paraphrasing is the standard steganography defense, but its effect on legitimate-monitor recall is rarely measured. Tells defenders whether a trusted-paraphraser firewall helps or hurts honesty monitoring — strategically valuable, train-free infrastructure prototype.

**Relevant context:** Roger & Greenblatt (arXiv 2310.18512) show paraphrasing defeats steganography; 'Gaming the Judge' (arXiv 2601.14691) shows unfaithful CoT fools judges. Whether paraphrasing also degrades honest monitoring of cue-use is an under-tested trade-off.
